title: Clarify that fodder relief leaves the ridge descent alarm unchanged
body: Four retained Claude playtests (three Sonnet 5 runs on published builds 24a036e1 and 0d2ed693, and an Opus 5 reference run on b7dd890e) reported ambiguity about fodder relief and the ridge descent alarm. Source review confirms that descending the exposed ridge adds 1 alarm, while relief fodder suppresses the separate increase only when the first LURE feed succeeds. The opening preview says On the Exposed Ridge, which blurs that sequence, and the trigger uses an ambiguous its. Clarify the feed-specific benefit and state that descent still adds 1 alarm. All four reports come from the Claude lineage; the Opus run is reference-tier support under the repository's triage rules. This is a wording clarification; the mechanics are already consistent. The latest Sonnet interview confused the fodder benefit with the final Aid-Only benefit. Its retained tool results show alarm 0 to 1 on the ridge, unchanged at 1 on successful first LAY, 1 to 2 on the second feed, and unchanged at 2 on the final feed under the distinct limited-duty herd-count rule. There was no refund or delayed fodder effect; this observation supports clarifying wording, not changing mechanics.

evidence.summary: Four retained playtests reported ambiguity; source review and captured action results confirm separate ridge, first-feed fodder, and final-feed Aid-Only effects.
